note: Initializes the output buffer size to 100 bytes; the buffer is allocated with xmlMallocAtomic(buffer_size).
Allocates the 100-byte output buffer; out is set to point at buffer start.
Parses a character reference like &#x...; or &#...; and returns the code point value; on malformed input it returns 0.
Writes the first byte of the decoded character into the output buffer BEFORE any buffer-growth check; if the buffer is nearly full this write can exceed the allocated region.
For c < 0x80 only one byte is written; for larger c values up to 4 bytes are written in the loop below.
Writes continuation bytes for multi-byte UTF-8 encodings; these writes also occur before the growth check, so a 4-byte character can overflow a buffer that is within 4 bytes of full.

The growth check happens only AFTER the character bytes were already written; the 100-byte margin is intended to prevent overflow but the write-before-check ordering leaves a window where the buffer can be overrun.
In the non-entity branch, reads the current input character; if the input is malformed UTF-8, htmlCurrentChar may return an uninitialized value from the encoding_error path.
Writes the possibly-uninitialized character value into the output buffer, propagating the uninitialized data into the attribute value string.

Terminates the attribute value string and returns it; the uninitialized bytes written earlier are now part of the returned string, leading to use-of-uninitialized-value and potential out-of-bounds reads downstream.
